analysis: Examined the changes to threat-model-review.yml, the new changelog fragment and the docs/developer/build.md CI documentation rewrite. None touch provider runtime code, keys, attestation or the coordinator/provider wire, so the provider-side threat IDs (TB-002/003/007/011, T-041 and others) are unaffected. In the workflow, the trigger changes to `pull_request_target: [labeled]` gated on the `run-threat-model` label (line 71). The runners move from Blacksmith to `ubuntu-24.04`, and `issues: write` is added (line 58) to allow the label-removal API call. The scanner is still checked out from the default branch (lines 83-90), not the PR head, and the PR is treated as data, so the pull_request_target pattern is not weakened. The new `issues: write` grant is a small permission broadening. It is only reachable in a job that already holds contents: write and id-token: write, and it runs trusted default-branch code. The one concern is the removal of the skipped-success guard in clearance mode (line 71), reported as a low finding. Remaining uncertainty: whether THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE is enabled with a required-check rule, and how GitHub attaches pull_request_target checks to the PR head. The changelog and build.md edits are documentation. Their claims about ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml and the other workflows (opt-in `run-ci` labels, tested-tree dedup, route retries, watchdog) could not be verified because those workflow files are not in this batch, so another pass should review them for permission or trigger regressions.

findings.detail: The old `if` carried a comment that, in clearance mode, an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success. The new `if` (line 71) only runs the job when the label is `run-threat-model`, and the trigger is now `types: [labeled]` (line 6). With THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=true, any other label event on a new head SHA makes the `review` job skip, and GitHub treats a skipped job as a passing required check. A user with triage rights (or automation) could add an unrelated label after a push or a failed run, so a required threat-model check could show as skipped/green with no `threat-review-gate.py after` evaluation. Fix: when clearance is required, keep the job running for every event and fail or pend closed unless the run-threat-model label is present, or run the gate in a separate job that always executes. Whether this applies depends on how the required-check rule is configured, which is not visible here.
findings.title: Clearance mode: unrelated label now yields a skipped (passing) job in place of a clearance run
